metadata.title: कोच राजवंशी : आदिवासी या क्षत्रिय | Koch-Rajbongshi : Tribal or kshatriyas
metadata.description: The Assam government recent decision to declare the Koch-Rajbongshi community as a protected class has sparked discontent on multiple fronts. While the move aims to provide certain safeguards and recognition, it falls short of the community’s long-standing demand for inclusion in the Scheduled Tribes (ST) list. As a result, many within the Koch-Rajbongshi community feel dissatisfied, viewing the “protected” status as a symbolic gesture rather than a meaningful change. On the other hand, several indigenous communities in Assam have opposed the decision, fearing it may dilute their rights and entitlements. They argue that the Koch-Rajbongshi’s new status could increase competition over limited resources and benefits reserved for indigenous groups. The issue underscores the complex social dynamics in Assam, where identity, recognition, and access to constitutional safeguards remain deeply contested. The decision has reignited debates over tribal classification and the politics of inclusion in the state.
